item.name: Quickstart
item.description: Start here. The first three requests confirm wiring; the rest are organised by OpenAPI tag (Discovery, Applications, Components, …).

request.description: Liveness probe. Open — no auth required.
Live OpenAPI spec. This collection is auto-derived from it.
Single-shot topology snapshot — apps, components, infra, connections.

description.content: Returns every Application in the graph with a `componentCount` of contained Components, ordered by tier then name.
Creates a new Application node. `tier` is required; reasonable defaults are filled in for `availability` (`99.9`) and `confidentiality` (`internal`).
Resolves the path param against `id` (UUID) or `name` and returns the Application + its Components + their owned Infra. Returns 404 when no match.
Any subset of the create fields. Unspecified fields keep their existing values via `coalesce`.

item.name: Delete an Application (cascades exclusively-owned Components + Infra)

request.name: Delete an Application (cascades exclusively-owned Components + Infra)

description.content: Removes the Application plus any Components that *only* belong to it, plus Infra that is *only* owned by those Components. Shared resources are preserved.

item.name: Application topology — Components, Infra, intra-app connections

request.name: Application topology — Components, Infra, intra-app connections

description.content: Returns the Application, every Component it contains, the Infra each Component is deployed on, and Component↔Component `:CONNECTS_TO` edges (with protocol/port).

response.name: Default Response

description.content: Walks each Component in the Application and lists Components in *other* Applications it has a `:CONNECTS_TO` edge to. Used by the impact-radius views.
Single source of truth for component types, tiers, environments, availability SLAs, and confidentiality levels. UI consumers fetch this once and hydrate dropdowns.

response.name: Default Response

description.content: Returns every Component with its containing Application (when one exists). Filterable via the `type` query (api / db / worker / ui).
Creates a Component node, optionally attaching it to an existing Application via `:CONTAINS`. Either `applicationId` or `appId` works (legacy alias).
Returns the Component, its parent Application (or null), and the Infra resources it owns via `:CONNECTS_TO {via:"component-mapping"}`.
Partial update on `name` / `type` / `runtime`. Other fields preserved.
DETACH-delete: removes every relationship the Component participates in (including ownership and Component↔Component connections).

item.name: Connect this Component to another (Component → Component edge)

request.name: Connect this Component to another (Component → Component edge)

description.content: Idempotently MERGEs a `:CONNECTS_TO {protocol, port}` edge from this Component to the target. No `via` is set — the endpoint labels (`:Component`→`:Component`) distinguish it from infra-side edges.

item.name: Deploy a Component onto an Infra (manual ownership)

request.name: Deploy a Component onto an Infra (manual ownership)

description.content: Idempotently MERGEs a `:CONNECTS_TO {via:"component-mapping", source:"manual-deploy", confidence:100}` edge from the Component to the Infra. Use this to record human-confirmed ownership.
Returns every Infra node, ordered by provider then name. Filterable by `provider` (aws/azure/gcp) and `public` (true/false).
Most Infra comes from discovery scans (`/discovery/scan/*`). Use this for resources that aren't in any cloud-API surface — e.g. an on-prem appliance you want represented in the graph.
Returns the Infra plus its `deployments` — every Component that owns it (with the containing Application name when available).

item.name: Update an Infra node (name / region / public flag)

request.name: Update an Infra node (name / region / public flag)

description.content: DETACH-deletes the node and every relationship it participates in. The next discovery scan will re-create it if it still exists in the cloud.

item.name: Infra owned by more than one Application (shared services)

request.name: Infra owned by more than one Application (shared services)

description.content: Returns Infra nodes whose owning Components live in two or more distinct Applications, ordered by `usedByApps` desc. Useful for surfacing shared services that need coordination during change windows.
Returns every Infra node flagged `public: true` plus the names of any Components that own them. Cross-cuts the security review surface.

item.name: Counts: applications, components, infra, connections, public-exposed

request.name: Counts: applications, components, infra, connections, public-exposed

description.content: A single-shot summary of the graph: total counts plus components-by-type and infra-by-provider histograms. Used by dashboard tiles.

item.name: Full graph snapshot — apps, components, connections, deployments, infra

request.name: Full graph snapshot — apps, components, connections, deployments, infra

description.content: Single response covering every Application, Component, Component↔Component connection (with protocol/port), Component→Infra deployment, and the unique Infra referenced. Drives the topology canvas.

response.name: Default Response

item.name: Blast-radius for a single Infra resource

request.name: Blast-radius for a single Infra resource

description.content: Walks Infra ← Component ← Application and returns every Component / Application that depends on the given Infra. Applications come back sorted by tier (1 = critical first).

item.name: Every Component → Component edge that crosses an Application boundary

request.name: Every Component → Component edge that crosses an Application boundary

description.content: Returns one row per cross-application Component connection: `from` (app, tier, component), `connection` (protocol, port), `to` (app, tier, component). Used for change-coordination dashboards.
Returns the shortest directed path of any relationship type from `from` to `to`, with the node sequence and hop count. 404 when no path exists.
Returns every saved snapshot, newest first. Snapshots are point-in-time captures of node counts; useful for diffing before/after a deploy.
Creates a `:Snapshot` node with the current node counts and an optional `label`. Snapshots are append-only — there's no DELETE endpoint.

item.name: Import a Terraform / OpenTofu state file (multipart upload)

request.name: Import a Terraform / OpenTofu state file (multipart upload)

description.content: Send `multipart/form-data` with a `statefile` field containing the `.tfstate` JSON. Resources are parsed via `parseTerraformState` and ingested into Neo4j as Infra nodes. Returns the import-job id, parse summary, and per-status counts.
Returns up to 20 import jobs newest-first with status, parsed Terraform version, workspace, resource counts, and total duration.
Returns every cloud account row with its decrypted `config` (the on-disk row stores AES-256-GCM-encrypted secrets — clientSecret, secretAccessKey, private_key — which are decrypted on read).

request.name: List enabled cloud accounts for a provider

description.content: Any subset of `name` / `config` / `enabled`. The `config` shape is *merged* into the existing decrypted config and re-encrypted, so you can patch one secret without re-supplying the others.
Removes the Postgres row. Discovery-emitted Infra nodes already in Neo4j are *not* deleted; they'll be marked stale on the next scan that runs without this account.

item.name: One-time migration: copy CloudAccount nodes from Neo4j to Postgres

request.name: One-time migration: copy CloudAccount nodes from Neo4j to Postgres

description.content: For graphs that pre-date the Postgres backing store. Idempotent (`ON CONFLICT (provider, name) DO UPDATE`). Returns the count of accounts migrated.

item.name: Internal — record a scan outcome on a cloud account

request.name: Internal — record a scan outcome on a cloud account

description.content: Called by the scan handlers in discovery.js to stamp `last_scan_at / last_scan_status / last_scan_total / last_scan_error` on the account row. Not typically called directly by external consumers.

item.name: Get the active cloud-AI provider configuration

request.name: Get the active cloud-AI provider configuration

description.content: Returns the saved Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini / Azure-OpenAI config with `apiKey` masked. Returns `{ configured: false }` when no config exists.
Replaces any existing config (only one active at a time). `apiKey` is AES-256-GCM-encrypted before INSERT. Setting Azure also requires `azureEndpoint` and `azureDeployment`.

item.name: Delete the saved cloud-AI provider configuration

request.name: Delete the saved cloud-AI provider configuration

description.content: After deletion `fastify.ai.refreshCloudFromDb()` clears the in-memory provider so subsequent `/ai/*` routes return 503 until a new config is saved.
Sends a trivial "Reply with exactly: OK" message and returns the provider response. Useful for verifying credentials without spending tokens on a real query.
Returns every row from the `integrations` table — ServiceNow, Terraform Cloud, OTel ingest, IaC state backends, etc. Secret fields are decrypted; client UIs are responsible for further obscuring.

Body shape: `{ type, name, config, enabled?, pollIntervalSeconds? }`. The `type` must match a registered connector (`/connectors`); the connector's `beforeUpsert` runs before validation to fill defaults / auto-generate secrets, and `afterUpsert` runs after persist to sync derived rows. Secret fields are AES-256-GCM-encrypted before INSERT.
Returns the integration row with config decrypted. Use `/connectors/:type` for the connector's schema and capabilities.
Patches `config` (merged + re-encrypted), `enabled`, or `pollIntervalSeconds`. The connector's before/afterUpsert hooks run on each update.
Removes the row. Resources the connector previously ingested into Neo4j stay; the next discovery sweep / cleanupStaleNodes will mark them stale.
Invokes `spec.healthCheck()` against the live integration. Returns `{ ok, detail }`. Cheap — does not ingest anything.
Runs `fetch → normalize → ingest` for the connector and records a `sync_jobs` row with the outcome. Returns the result envelope (resourcesFound / created / updated / warnings).
Returns up to 50 of the most recent `sync_jobs` rows for this integration with status, durations, and per-status counts. Use this to debug why an ingest didn't produce the expected nodes.

Pages every aggregated resource via `SelectAggregateResourceConfig` and writes Infra + structural `:CONNECTS_TO` edges. With a body, runs a one-off scan against the supplied credentials; without one, scans every enabled AWS account from `/integrations/cloud`. Requires `aggregatorName` + `aggregatorRegion` (or `AWS_CONFIG_AGGREGATOR_NAME` env var). See [docs/aws-config-aggregator-coverage.md](../docs/aws-config-aggregator-coverage.md).

Pages a single ARG KQL query and writes Infra + structural `:CONNECTS_TO` edges. With a body, runs a one-off scan against the supplied subscription/credentials; without one, scans every enabled Azure account from `/integrations/cloud`. See [docs/azure-resource-graph-coverage.md](../docs/azure-resource-graph-coverage.md).

item.name: Scan GCP via Cloud Asset Inventory

request.name: Scan GCP via Cloud Asset Inventory

description.content: Pages `cloudasset.assets.listAssets` for the project and writes Infra + structural `:CONNECTS_TO` edges. With a body, runs a one-off scan; without one, scans every enabled GCP account from `/integrations/cloud`. See [docs/gcp-cloud-asset-coverage.md](../docs/gcp-cloud-asset-coverage.md).

item.name: Scan every configured cloud account in parallel

request.name: Scan every configured cloud account in parallel

description.content: Fans out to `scanAWS` / `scanAzure` / `scanGCP` for every enabled account configured at `/integrations/cloud`. Bootstrap runs once at the end; cleanup is per-provider. The single response covers all three clouds with per-account breakdowns under `results.<provider>[]`.
Returns the cron-style schedule plus the last-run / next-run timestamps. The scheduler runs every enabled provider in parallel.
Replaces the schedule with `{ enabled, cron }`. The cron string is standard 5-field; consult any cron reference. Setting `enabled: false` disables future runs without deleting the config.
Equivalent to `POST /discovery/scan/all` but uses the same code path the scheduler does (so it picks up the same accounts + flags).

Returns the Infra node plus every `:CONNECTS_TO` edge it participates in (incoming and outgoing), with full edge properties. Use this to understand why the suggest engine made a particular call. **Admin-tier only**, and in production must also have `APPCLOUD_DEBUG=1` set.

item.name: Pull the suggest engine's current output

request.name: Pull the suggest engine's current output

description.content: For every unmapped Infra, returns up to 5 ranked Component candidates with rule names + scores. Drives the mapping-suggestions UI.

item.name: Apply a batch of confirmed mappings (legacy single-action endpoint)

request.name: Apply a batch of confirmed mappings (legacy single-action endpoint)

description.content: Each mapping creates a `:CONNECTS_TO {via:"component-mapping", source:"auto-mapped"}` edge. For mixed-action batches (link + create-component + create-application), use `/discovery/suggest/apply-all`.

item.name: Apply a mixed-action batch from the suggest engine

request.name: Apply a mixed-action batch from the suggest engine

description.content:
Three action shapes share one endpoint:
- `link_component` — link existing Component to existing Infra
- `create_component` — create a Component under an existing Application + link
- `create_application` — create Application + Component(s) + link

Phase 2 also runs after the batch: tag-based auto-link sweeps any still-unmapped Infra against the newly-created components.

item.name: Refresh tags for a single Infra (currently a hint)

request.name: Refresh tags for a single Infra (currently a hint)

description.content: Per-resource refresh is not yet implemented — the response is a `hint` instructing the caller to run a full provider scan. Reserved for a future targeted fetch.
Filterable by `provider` and `resourceType`. Each row has `mapped: bool` indicating whether at least one Component owns it via `:CONNECTS_TO {via:"component-mapping"}`.

item.name: Discovery summary — counts by provider and type

request.name: Discovery summary — counts by provider and type

description.content: For each (provider, resource_type) pair, returns total + mapped count. Drives the discovery dashboard.

item.name: Manually link an Infra to a Component

request.name: Manually link an Infra to a Component

description.content: Idempotent MERGE of `:CONNECTS_TO {via:"component-mapping", source:"manual-link", confidence:100}`. Use this when the suggest engine missed a mapping.
Refuses (409) when any Component owns the Infra. Unlink first via `DELETE` on the owning Component's connection or use `/discovery/resources/bulk-delete` with explicit confirmation.

item.name: Delete multiple Infra resources by id

request.name: Delete multiple Infra resources by id

description.content: Per-id behavior matches `DELETE /discovery/resources/:id`: linked Infra is skipped (with reason), unlinked is removed. The response details deleted / skipped / errored.

item.name: Run bootstrap (tag + RG-propagation auto-link) without scanning

request.name: Run bootstrap (tag + RG-propagation auto-link) without scanning

description.content: Useful when you've added/edited tags in the cloud and want to re-derive Application/Component mappings without paying for a full scan. Episode-tracked.

Returns the available enrichment strategies for Azure (resource-graph / network-watcher / monitor-insights / tagging / azure-arc / name-heuristics) with descriptions, required permissions, and token cost. Drives the strategy selector in `/discovery/enrich/azure`.

item.name: Run Azure supplement layers (Network Watcher / VM Insights / auto-link)

request.name: Run Azure supplement layers (Network Watcher / VM Insights / auto-link)

description.content: Invokes one of the named strategies from `/discovery/linking-strategies` against the configured Azure account. Idempotent — safe to re-run. `monitor-insights` requires a Log Analytics workspace ID; `network-watcher` requires Network Watcher Reader.
Returns the static list of providers AppCloud can scan (aws / azure / gcp) with display metadata. UI uses this to render the provider picker.
Returns the per-provider, typed-label catalogue derived from `discovery.schema.js`. Includes the cross-cloud ontology label (e.g. `ComputeInstance` covers Azure VM, EC2, GCE) and an icon hint.

Every mutation API call writes a row here. `actor` is exact-match by default — pass `?like=true` to opt into the legacy substring/ILIKE behaviour (separate keys with similar names like `ci-deploy-staging` / `ci-deploy-prod` previously collapsed into one query, which is now opt-in). Other filters: `action`, `resourceType`, `resourceId`, `keyId` (exact UUID), `scope` (admin|write|read), `from`/`to` (ISO date), `q` (substring on `resource_name` OR `actor`). Returns `{ rows, total, page, pageSize, pages }`. Each row includes `actorKeyId` and `actorScope` so a row can be traced back to the specific API key that performed the action.

query.description: Exact match by default. Set `like=true` for case-insensitive substring (legacy).
Opt-in substring match for `actor` (default false = exact match).
Exact match on actor_key_id — see GET /admin/api-keys for ids.

item.name: Audit-log analytics for the last N days

request.name: Audit-log analytics for the last N days

description.content: Returns counts grouped by action / resource_type / actor plus a daily-activity series for sparklines. Default window is 30 days; pass `?days=N` to widen.

item.name: Full audit history for a specific resource

request.name: Full audit history for a specific resource

description.content: Up to the last 500 events for one (resource_type, resource_id) pair, newest first. `resource_type` is one of `Application`, `Component`, `Infra`, `CloudAccount`, etc.

item.name: All audit events by a specific actor (paginated)

request.name: All audit events by a specific actor (paginated)

description.content: Exact match on the `actor` column by default. Pass `?like=true` for case-insensitive substring (legacy behaviour, collapses across similarly-named keys). Optional `?keyId=<uuid>` narrows to a specific stored API key (exact match on actor_key_id) — preferable to substring-name matching once you know the key id. Optional `?scope=admin|write|read` narrows to one privilege tier.

query.description: Opt-in substring match (default false = exact match).

description.content: Returns whether the local provider (Ollama) and the cloud provider (Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini / Azure) are reachable, plus model + baseUrl. Used by the UI to gate AI-feature affordances.

item.name: Plain-English explanation for a mapping suggestion

request.name: Plain-English explanation for a mapping suggestion

description.content: Given an Infra + a candidate Component mapping (output of `/discovery/suggest`), the local LLM produces a human-readable rationale. Useful for tooltips on suggestion cards.

item.name: AI-augmented Application/Component scoring for one Infra

request.name: AI-augmented Application/Component scoring for one Infra

description.content: Given an Infra id, returns LLM-scored candidate Applications. Complements the rule-based scores from the suggest engine; clients combine both.

item.name: Plain-English blast-radius narrative for one Infra

request.name: Plain-English blast-radius narrative for one Infra

description.content: Walks the impact graph (same shape as `/graph/impact`), then asks the local LLM to summarise the change risk in one paragraph. Use this in the impact-review surface.

item.name: High-level architectural plan over the whole graph (cloud LLM)

request.name: High-level architectural plan over the whole graph (cloud LLM)

description.content: Fetches a graph snapshot (apps, infra summary, cross-app dependencies) and asks the configured cloud LLM for an architectural review. Returns 503 when no cloud AI is configured.

item.name: Remediation plan for unmapped/drifted Infra (cloud LLM)

request.name: Remediation plan for unmapped/drifted Infra (cloud LLM)

description.content: Without a body, picks up to 50 unmapped discovered Infra nodes and asks the cloud LLM to propose mappings or tag changes. With a body, scores the supplied items.
Pulls `/graph/topology` and asks the cloud LLM to flag risky dependency patterns (single points of failure, cycles, tier-skipping calls). Returns 503 when no cloud AI is configured.

item.name: Conversational chat with live graph context

request.name: Conversational chat with live graph context

description.content: Injects a fresh snapshot of applications + infra + unmapped resources + cross-app deps into the system prompt before forwarding the conversation. Returns the assistant's reply plus a reference to the context used.
Generates a fresh `ak_…` plaintext, stores SHA-256(plaintext) + the requested scopes, and returns the plaintext **once**. Save it immediately — it is never recoverable.
Returns every row including revoked ones, sorted by creation time (newest first). Plaintext is **never** returned — only the prefix and metadata.
Soft-deletes the key by setting `revoked_at = now()`. Bootstrap rows (env-var-derived) cannot be revoked here — rotate the env var instead.

item.name: Update an API key (name / scopes / expiresAt)

request.name: Update an API key (name / scopes / expiresAt)

description.content: Updates the row metadata. The secret cannot be patched — generate a new key and revoke the old one. Bootstrap rows are read-only. Pass `expiresAt: null` to clear an expiry, or an ISO instant to set/extend.

Returns every connector registered with the framework — ServiceNow, Terraform Cloud, OTel ingest, IaC state backends. Each entry includes its `authSchema`, `configSchema`, and UI metadata. Use this to render dynamic connector-creation forms.
Returns the full spec for one connector — `id`, `displayName`, `description`, JSON schemas for auth + config, UI metadata, capabilities. Used by the connector-creation UI to drive a form.

info.name: AppCloud API
info.description:
Generated from docs/openapi.yaml via `npm run openapi:export`.

## Setup
1. Set `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:3000`) and `apiKey`
2. Hit `Quickstart → GET /health`
3. Walk the per-tag folders for full CRUD coverage

For narrative workflow recipes, see `docs/api-guide.md §13`.
